notes:
SUMMARY: Mid-market B2B SaaS (workflow automation) evaluating Redwood for chat/agent features. Primary drive = reduce engineering ops for agent orchestration and meet firm latency SLOs for customer-facing assistants. Started hosted API POC with streaming + function/tool-calls; later interested in Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost controls.

RECENT TIMELINE: 
- 2026-01-20: Intro discovery call (Jordan + Maya) — high-level use case: multi-step agentic workflows (search -> extract -> act). Customer quote: "need deterministic latency in production — streaming must feel realtime".
- 2026-02-10: Product demo (streaming + tool-calls example) — showed function-calling flow for ticket triage, demo used hosted model with SSE stream.
- 2026-02-28: POC kickoff (hosted API) — baseline: 1) streaming SSE + incremental tokens for UI 2) function calls to internal search and actions service 3) obs hooks for per-token and per-call latency.
- 2026-03-03: POC run notes — initial throughput OK but observed tool-call tail latency spikes (search API sometimes >800ms), causing perceived lag in UI and occasional agent timeouts. Logged INF-1123.
- 2026-03-05: Deep-dive with SE (Maya) — tested fallback to faster small model for summarization step; experimented with prefetching search results before model step. Fireflies ff-20260305-7691.
- 2026-03-11: Security intake submitted; awaiting SOC2 artefacts and clarification on residency for EU customers.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS / NOTES: 
- Workload: interactive multi-step agents; must support streaming tokens + function/tool-calling (search + action).
- Latency SLO: interactive UI wants p95 <= 300ms; internal target p95 for model-only token generation ~150-200ms, but acceptable to route to faster variant for non-critical steps.
- Tool-call reliability: primary concern. Need: per-tool-call timeout controls, retry/backoff semantics, idempotency tokens, circuit-breaker metrics. Want instrumentation: per-tool latency, retries, failed-call histogram, instance-level KV cache hit rates.
- Fallbacks: desire automated model fallback (e.g., route to quantized/fast variant when long-tail tool calls degrade end-to-end latency). Prefer policy-driven routing (latency-first vs cost-first).
- Streaming behaviour: must support chunked function call payloads and progressive tool results to feed the model without blocking UI.
- Caching/batching: interested in prefix caching and prefetch for common queries; batching needs to preserve low-latency tail.

BUSINESS / PROCUREMENT: 
- Interested in trying Hosted API for POC, then evaluating Dedicated reserved capacity if traffic justifies. Need a TCO comparison (per-token hosted vs committed dedicated nodes) — asked for 12/24 month scenarios.
- Procurement timeline: aiming to decide on dedicated commitment by 2026-04 if POC latency issues resolvable.

OPEN ITEMS / BLOCKERS: 
- Security questions outstanding (data residency for EU customers).
- Need explicit design for tool-call retries and agent idempotency to avoid duplicate actions.
- Pricing delta: customer wants clear committed capacity pricing and overage rules.

ACTION ITEMS / NEXT STEPS: 
- Redwood: produce pricing proposal + 12/24 month TCO for dedicated nodes (Jordan).
- SE (Maya): infra deep-dive session on 2026-03-18 to demo circuit-breaker config, per-tool metrics and show model-fallback in a canary.
- Customer: provide representative load trace and list of third-party tool endpoints to simulate in POC.

ADDITIONAL REFERENCES: Jira INF-1123 (timeout spikes), drive pricing deck, security FAQ link above. Notes contain shorthand logs from POC sessions; some gaps in timestamps and raw logs attached in drive link.
